chunks: Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Zurara, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem with killing the flea, and the louse, and the bug inside the Haram.
ai.seo_question: What insects can be killed while in Ihram inside the Haram without penalty?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via Zurarah, clarifies that the general prohibition on killing game in Ihram does not extend to small, non-game insects like fleas, lice, and bedbugs, even within the sanctified boundaries of the Haram. This ruling highlights the juristic distinction between 'game' (dawāb) and common pests, ensuring that the pilgrim's ritual state remains uncompromised by minor nuisances. It reflects the practical flexibility (rukhas) embedded in Shia fiqh to facilitate worship without undue hardship.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem with killing the flea, and the louse, and the bug inside the Harram’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ahmad has narrated from ibn Faddal from certain persons of our people from Zurarah who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not harmful to kill a flea, louse or a bedbug in al- Haram (the sacred area).”’
